newsitem.title: UK: Boeing fires first salvo in airshow sales duel.
newsitem.headline: Boeing fires first salvo in airshow sales duel.

text.p: Boeing Co scored the first hit in its traditional airshow feud against arch rival Airbus Industrie on Monday in a carefully packaged salvo of sales valued at $6.3 billion.
Boeing Commercial Airplane Group president Ron Woodard announced the bundle of sales for 68 aircraft to seven airlines and leasing companies at a news conference.

Airbus was left stranded, having to postpone its own news conference which was due to take place immediately after Boeing's when the floor of the press room collapsed under the sheer weight of journalists.

The Boeing deals announced just before the mishap included an $800 million launch order for Boeing's new 757-300 stretch version of its medium range twinjet from German holiday airline Condor Flugdienst. The carrier is acquiring 12 of the new aircraft and has taken options on a further 12.
British Airways ordered four more 747-400s, three 777-200s and three 757-200s and in addition brought forward delivery dates for 10 more 747-400s to replace its older 747-100s.
Australian leasing firm Ansett Worldwide is acquiring 16 737s and nine 767-300ERs while U.S. leasing giant International Lease Finance Company is buying five each of the 757 767 and 737 types.

Meanwhile Danish carrier Maersk Air has ordered three 737- 500s, Polish airline LOT is acquiring two 737-400s and one 767- 300ER. British holiday firm Airtours is also acquiring a 767-300ER and Air Berlin has ordered a 737-400.
